source_text: Orationes contra Arianos (fragmenta) ΟΙ ΛΟΓΟΙ ΚΑΤΑ ΑΡΕΙΑΝΩΝ 54 Ἀλλ' οἱ παράδοξοι τῆς Ἀρείου θυμέλης μεσόχοροι τὸ μὲν ἁμαρτίαν πεποιηκέναι τὸν Χριστὸν φράζουσι· 55 Τὸ δὲ ὅτι Θεὸς ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ κόσμον καταλλάσσων ἑαυτῷ, οὔτε ἐν μνήμῃ φέρουσιν οὔτε τοῖς τῆς γλώττης ὀργάνοις
orientation: Eustathius is describing how the Arians quote only part of a scriptural passage about Christ, saying he committed sin while omitting the words that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself.
pass_a_gloss: But the strange mid-chorus [members] of the band of Arius say, on the one hand, that Christ committed sin; but on the other hand, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, they neither hold in memory nor [utter] with the instruments of the tongue.

choices.english: strange mid-chorus members of the band of Arius
choices.why: Keeps the theatrical metaphor of a chorus or troupe, which Eustathius uses to mock the Arians as performers rather than teachers.
Required glossary rendering; keeps the perfect infinitive force of a completed act.
Required glossary rendering; preserves the participial construction and the reflexive dative.
Literal rendering of the idiom φέρειν ἐν μνήμῃ, keeping the verb 'hold' to show the mental retention Eustathius denies them.

choices.english: with the instruments of the tongue
choices.why: Literal rendering of the physiological metaphor for speech organs; the sentence continues in the next section with the verb.

bible_refs.note: Θεὸς ἦν ἐν Χριστῷ κόσμον καταλλάσσων ἑαυτῷ

pass_b_english: The strange mid-chorus members of Arius's troupe say that Christ committed sin. But the words that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself (2 Corinthians 5:19) they neither hold in memory nor speak with the instruments of the tongue.

last_rejected.ruling: Source has no ἐκφωνοῦσιν; text reads φέρουσιν. 'Speak' renders the context adequately.
